sonnet.problem: The joke 'uh-oh, now the LORD has plans too' plays on God's own plan of judgment and gives Him a comedic, reactive tone. The joke is about God's action instead of staying on the human side of the moment.
sonnet.rule: Jokes never put words, tones or reactions in God's or Jesus' mouth, never cast him in God's role, and never play on a name or title of God... Comparisons stay on the human side of the moment.

sonnet.problem: The question states the gathering as already done ('The gathered remnant is brought together'). Micah 2:12 is a promise: 'I will bring them together'.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The question narrates a future promise as something happening now ('they break through the ___ and go out by it'). The text says 'they will break through the gate'.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The question puts a prophecy in the present tense ('As they go out, who passes through before them'). The text says 'Their King will pass through before them'.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."
